title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Pricing, Case Studies, and Security FAQ
author: Jordan Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s core positioning and messaging, competitive brief summaries, pitch deck guidance, pricing guidance, representative case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospect conversations. It is intended for sales, solutions engineering, and customer success teams as a single source of truth for pre-sales and early onboarding conversations.

Use this document to:
- Align on top-line value props and objection responses.
- Assemble pitch decks quickly using recommended messaging and one-page customer examples.
- Answer security questions consistently during RFPs and prospect calls.

1) Positioning & Messaging

Top-line positioning (elevator):
Redwood Inference: a production-first inference platform that makes LLM-powered applications predictable, low-cost, and reliable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Primary customer problems we solve:
- Variable latency and high per-token cost at scale.
- Operational complexity of self-hosted inference (deployments, upgrades, fallback).
- Data residency and compliance requirements for regulated workloads.

Key message pillars (use these as lead-ins in decks and discovery):
- Production performance: predictable latency and throughput with GPU-optimized serving runtime. Call out: continuous batching, KV/prefix caching, and model-architecture-aware kernel selection.
- Cost controls: intelligent batching, quantization recommendations, and routing policies that reduce per-token unit economics. Provide example: typical mid-market customers reduce inference cost 25-40% after adopting Redwood Optimize profiles.
- Deployment flexibility: same API and tooling across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments — zero-code rollout changes.
- Reliability & graceful degradation: automated fallbacks (model variants, regions, capacity tiers) and SLA-backed Dedicated options.
- Developer experience: fast onboarding, first-class SDKs, streaming/responses and function-calling support.

Message examples by persona:
- Product / Engineering: “Run large-scale inference with predictable latency and per-token cost — we handle caching, batching and routing so you can move faster.”
- Platform / Infra: “Deliver a single interface across hosted and private environments that respects your network and compliance constraints.”
- Security / Compliance: “Private deployment and VPC options with audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations and configurable retention windows.”

2) Competitive Briefs (high-level)

Summary format: Strength | Weakness | Typical customer fit

Competitor A: Large cloud AI endpoints
- Strength: Deep cloud integrations, global regions, and managed infra.
- Weakness: Limited control over inference economics, less transparent per-token performance profiles, and slower feature rollout cadence.
- Typical fit: Customers who prioritize deep cloud-native integration above inference unit economics.

Competitor B: LLM API providers (simplicity-first)
- Strength: Extremely simple API, broad model catalog.
- Weakness: Higher cost per token at scale; fewer private deployment options and limited enterprise SLAs.
- Typical fit: Low-volume experimentation or proof-of-concept teams.

Competitor C: Self-hosted inference runtimes/orchestration vendors
- Strength: Full control, potentially lower infra cost on committed hardware.
- Weakness: Heavy ops burden; requires in-house expertise for batching, kernel tuning, and reliability.
- Typical fit: Platform teams with existing GPU ops teams and strict data control needs that want to build in-house.

How to position against common objections:
- “We can host it ourselves.” -> Acknowledge control benefits, then highlight time-to-production and ongoing ops costs (kernel tuning, KV cache correctness, continuous batching). Share Redwood’s benchmark: median go-live time 6-8 weeks vs 3-6 months in self-hosted projects.
- “We use Provider X already.” -> Emphasize Redwood’s competitive advantage on unit economics and consistent tooling across private/hosted options; offer to run a 2-week cost/latency pilot using a customer workload.

3) Pitch Deck Guidance

Recommended deck structure (10-12 slides):
1. Title & one-line problem statement
2. Why it matters: business impact (latency, cost, reliability)
3. Customer example / testimonial (1-2 slides)
4. Product overview and deployment modes (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
5. Architecture snapshot (serving runtime, routing, caching)
6. Performance & cost differentiation (benchmarks)
7. Security & compliance highlights
8. Pricing & purchasing options (one-pager)
9. Implementation plan / timeline (pilot -> production)
10. Success metrics & support (SLA, onboarding, customer success)
11. Next steps / ask

Slide tips:
- Use real numbers when possible (latency p50/p95, unit cost delta, pilot timeline).
- Keep architecture slides high-level; include one “deep-dive” appendix slide for technical prospects.
- Include implementation checklist with ownership (SE, Eng, Customer).

Demo checklist for SEs (pre-demo prep):
- Confirm target models, typical sequence lengths, and expected QPS.
- Prepare a short workload-specific benchmark or live demo sample (30-90 seconds).
- Ensure security discussion is tailored to prospect’s environment (SaaS vs VPC vs on-prem).

4) Pricing Guidance (reference only)

Pricing principles:
- Transparent, usage-first pricing for Hosted (per-token / per-embedding) with volume tiers.
- Committed Reserved Capacity for Dedicated (monthly or annual) with guaranteed throughput and latency SLAs.
- Private deployments priced as platform license + deployment & support services.
- Value-based packaging: price based on predictable cost savings (batching/caching/quantization gains) and business-critical SLOs.

Reference pricing table (example ranges for prospects)
| Offer | Billing Model | Typical fit | Notes |
| Hosted API | Per-token / per-embed | Startups, low-to-medium QPS | Fastest time-to-value, self-serve |
| Dedicated | Monthly commit (GPU pools) | High throughput, enterprise | SLA-backed latency/uptime, predictable costs |
| Private | License + services | Regulated industries | VPC/on-prem options, KMS/HSM integrations |

Pricing negotiation playbook:
1. For mid-market: emphasize predictable unit cost and offer 3-month pilot credits combined with usage reporting.
2. For enterprise: shift to committed capacity conversation early; quantify cost and SLA delta vs hosted.
3. For strategic customers: offer custom success metrics, extended onboarding and dedicated SRE support as add-ons.

5) Case Studies (2 short vignettes for use in decks)

Case study: FinTech payments processor
- Problem: High variability in authorization latency and unpredictable inference spend for fraud models.
- Solution: Migrated fraud scoring to Redwood Dedicated, enabled KV caching for user histories, and configured routing to quantized variants for low-risk flows.
- Outcome: 35% reduction in per-transaction inference cost, p95 latency reduced from 520ms to 210ms, and measurable drop in false positives over 90 days.

Case study: Healthcare SaaS (HIPAA-regulated)
- Problem: Need private deployment with strict data residency and auditability for clinical note summarization.
- Solution: Deployed Redwood Private in customer VPC with KMS integration and custom retention windows; provided audit logs to compliance team.
- Outcome: Successful SOC2-type review; 2-week pilot, 6-week production rollout, and adoption by 3 product teams within 3 months.

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (concise answers for SEs and AE use)

Q: Where does customer data live when using Hosted API?
A: Customer data is processed in the selected region. For sensitive workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private which provide data isolation and optional customer-managed keys.

Q: Do you support KMS / HSM for key management?
A: Yes. Redwood Private and Dedicated integrations support cloud KMS or HSM solutions depending on deployment. We provide guidance for key rotation and access controls.

Q: How long are logs and request data retained?
A: Default retention is 30 days for Hosted. For Dedicated/Private, retention windows are configurable per contract; we can offer custom retention policies for compliance.

Q: Can we get audit logs for model inputs/outputs and admin actions?
A: Yes. We provide audit logs for admin actions and can capture request metadata. For output retention we support configurable levels and can redact or avoid persisting sensitive outputs.

Q: What certifications and compliance evidence do you provide?
A: We maintain SOC 2 Type II and provide compliance evidence packages; for regulated customers we run Private deployments and support contractual controls. See security-and-compliance/audit-logging for detailed artifacts.

Q: How do you handle vulnerability disclosures and incident response?
A: We operate a documented incident response process with security on-call rotations. We provide timely notifications per contractual SLAs and collaborate on remediation.

Security quick-reference table:
| Topic | Hosted | Dedicated | Private |
| Data residency | Region-based processing | Customer tenancy | Customer VPC / On-prem |
| KMS/HSM | Platform-managed KMS | Optional CMK | Customer-managed KMS/HSM |
| Audit logs | Basic request metadata | Extended logs (w/contract) | Full auditability |

7) Sales Objections & Suggested Responses

Objection: “Your platform sounds complex to operate.”
Suggested response: “We surface operational levers in Redwood Console and provide a prescriptive onboarding plan. Most customers go from pilot to production within 6-8 weeks with our SE + customer success support.”

Objection: “We’re concerned about vendor lock-in.”
Suggested response: “We support standard model formats (ONNX / HF) and provide exportable model/config artifacts. Our emphasis on consistent APIs across deployment modes reduces migration friction.”

8) Playbook: Discovery Questions & Next Steps

Discovery checklist (ask early in conversation):
- What model(s) are you using today and what are typical sequence lengths?
- Expected QPS and peak concurrency?
- Latency SLOs (p50 / p95) that matter for your product?
- Data residency, retention, and encryption requirements?
- Expected monthly inference volume (tokens / embeddings)?
- Who on your side owns infra/security/compliance approvals?

Suggested next steps after discovery:
1. Build a scoped pilot plan (2-4 weeks) that includes sample dataset, success metrics, and security baseline.
2. Run an initial benchmark (cost & latency) and share a one-page findings report.
3. Propose deployment option (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with pricing and timeline.
